text:
And you knew how to love, and you were prudent,

and it was spring and you were good,

and the sky was blue, resplendent.


And you kissed my hands with sweetness,

and looked into my eyes with your eyes,

which sometimes bit with bitterness.


And I passed by like ice itself...

I passed by without seeing where I was

neither the cruel hell nor the kindly sky.


I felt nothing... In the void

I wandered with the soul condemned

to my satanic and somber pain.


And I let you go silently,

you, who knew how to love and were good,

and were sweet, magnanimous and prudent.


Every pleading word was too little for you,

but pain closed my ears...

Ah, the soul was like hard rock.

translation.title: Aymé!
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated goodness of the beloved against the speaker's numbness.
